record.paper_title: Analysis on Faddeev Knots and Skyrme Solitons: Recent Progress and Open Problems
record.original_question: In the Faddeev model, finite-energy static fields are maps n: R^3 → S^2 with Hopf invariant Q(n)=N, and the corresponding Faddeev knots are energy-minimizing configurations in a fixed Hopf class. For each nonzero integer N, does there exist a finite-energy static map with Hopf invariant N that minimizes the Faddeev energy among all maps with that Hopf invariant?

evidence.quote: solution configurations of the Hopf charge Q from Q = 1 up to Q = 8 and found that, for Q = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, the energy-minimizing solitons are ring-shaped and higher charges cause greater distortion, and for Q = 6, 7, 8, the solitons become knotted or linked. In particular, the trefoil knot appears at Q = 7. Thus, as in the case of the Skyrme model, we are facing again a topologically constrained minimization problem and our ultimate question is to find out whether there is a static Faddeev energy minimizer among each topological class defined by a nontrivial Hopf index (charge).

The energy-minimizing maps in each topological class Q(n) = N are knotted solitons called the Faddeev knots [13, 14, 15, 32]. Hence we need to study the following topologically constrained minimization problem (3.24) EN = inf{E(n) | E(n) < ∞, Q(n) = N},

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider the Faddeev model on R^3 for unit-vector fields n: R^3 → S^2 ⊂ R^3 with n(x) → n_∞ as |x| → ∞ for some constant n_∞ ∈ S^2. For such a map, define the Faddeev energy
  E(n) = ∫_{R^3} ( Σ_{i=1}^{3} |∂_i n|^2 + Σ_{1 ≤ i < j ≤ 3} |∂_i n × ∂_j n|^2 ) dx.
Any finite-energy configuration n extends to a continuous map S^3 → S^2, and so carries a Hopf invariant Q(n) ∈ Z = π_3(S^2). Equivalently, writing F = n^* ω where ω is the area form on S^2, choose A on R^3 with dA = F; then
  Q(n) = (1/(16π^2)) ∫_{R^3} A ∧ dA.
For each integer N, define
  E_N = inf { E(n) : E(n) < ∞, Q(n) = N }.

Question. For every nonzero integer N, does there exist a finite-energy map n: R^3 → S^2 with Q(n) = N such that E(n) = E_N? That is, is the topologically constrained infimum E_N attained for every N ∈ Z \ {0}?
artifact.status_search_result: Lin and Yang (Comm. Math. Phys., 2004) proved that the infimum E_N is attained for an infinite subset of integers N, and in particular for the smallest nonzero |N|, but existence of a minimizer for every nonzero integer N on R^3 is not established. A substantial-inequality/energy-splitting framework (Lin–Yang) reduces full existence to ruling out energy splitting, which remains unresolved. Thus the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Existence of Energy Minimizers as Stable Knotted Solitons in the Faddeev Model
status_evidence.snippet: There exists an infinite subset S of Z such that for any m ∈ S the Faddeev energy has a minimizer in the topological class Q = m.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is established for infinitely many but not necessarily all Hopf classes.

status_evidence.title: Energy Splitting, Substantial Inequality, and Minimization for the Faddeev and Skyrme Models
status_evidence.snippet: Reduces the minimization in each Hopf class to a substantial inequality preventing energy splitting.
status_evidence.claim: Full existence for every N hinges on a substantial inequality that is not known in general.
